name: Dates
description: Dried dates represent the naturally dehydrated drupe fruits of Phoenix dactylifera, functioning as a dense carbohydrate-mineral hydro-matrix and an advanced cellular energy substrate. Structurally, the fibrous pericarp packages a highly concentrated, low-moisture pool of inverted monosaccharide enantiomers, seamlessly integrated within a resilient structural scaffold of non-starch polysaccharides and insoluble lignins. This botanical architecture retains a sophisticated profile of bound phenolic compounds, including hydrophilic ferulic and coumaric acids, alongside essential cellular electrolyte ions. Operating as a fast-acting metabolic fuel and cytoprotective superfood, its specific osmotic properties and soluble fibers slow down upper luminal irritation while driving immediate systemic glycogen synthesis and optimizing vascular smooth muscle homeostasis.
macroIntro: The macronutrient architecture of dried dates consists of a hyper-concentrated carbohydrate matrix dominated by instantly bioavailable simple hexoses, balanced by a minimal nitrogenous protein fraction.
microIntro: A highly concentrated mineral and organic assembly exceptionally rich in intracellular fluid regulators, enzymatic cofactors, and protective plant polyphenols.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: High thermodynamic energy density originating from the immediate conversion of simple hexose monosaccharides into cellular adenosine triphosphate.

macroNutrients.name: Total Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: A dense monosaccharide blend composed of free D-fructose and D-glucose, providing rapid substrate availability for cellular glycolysis.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Minimal vegetable protein fractions consisting of non-essential amino acids embedded within the cellular walls of the pulp.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Trace lipophilic compounds mostly comprising structural surface cuticular waxes and membrane phospholipids.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: A major intracellular cation critical for maintaining transmembrane resting potential, regulating blood volume, and driving myocardial polarization.

microNutrients.name: Polyphenols (Flavonoids)
microNutrients.description: Hydrophilic phenolic acids and proanthocyanidins that neutralize free radicals and suppress vascular endothelial lipid peroxidation cascades.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: A sophisticated network of beta-glucans, pectins, and insoluble cellulose that regulates bowel transit and feeds beneficial colonic microbiota.

microNutrients.name: Copper
microNutrients.description: An essential trace mineral cofactor required for cytochrome c oxidase function, iron assimilation, and cross-linking of dermal collagen fibers.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)
microNutrients.description: A vital water-soluble coenzyme that drives gluconeogenesis, amino acid transamination, and the synthesis of core neurotransmitters.

healthBenefits: Immediate Dual-Channel Glycolytic Flux and Energy Replenishment: The natural 1 to 1 balance of free D-glucose and D-fructose enables simultaneous transport via SGLT1 and GLUT5 intestinal enterocyte proteins, maximizing the velocity of hepatic glycogen synthesis.

Peristaltic Optimization via Insoluble Polysaccharide Matrix: High densities of non-digestible structural cellulose and lignins exert mechanical volumetric pressure along the colonic mucosal lining, accelerating transit dynamics to prevent chronic constipation.

Potassium-Mediated Vascular Hyperpolarization and Pressure Regulation: Elevated bioavailable potassium ions activate smooth muscle cell membrane channels, prompting intracellular hyperpolarization that causes vasodilation and a systemic down-regulation of arterial blood pressure.

Phenolic Attenuation of Mucosal Inflammatory Transcription: Native soluble polyphenols and tannins interact directly with free inflammatory radicals, directly intercepting oxidative stress cascades within the luminal epithelial layers.
precautionsIntro: Owing to the hyper-concentrated nature of its monosaccharide substrate and specific structural surface adhesive properties, date consumption requires targeted clinical management:
precautions: Substantial Caloric Payload and Adipose Homeostasis Strain: The elevated carbohydrate density per individual unit can rapidly generate a positive energy balance if volume is unmonitored, redirecting extra hexoses into hepatic triglyceride synthesis.

Accelerated Postprandial Glucose Influx and Insulin Demand: Exhibiting a moderate-to-high glycemic index, the rapid dissolution of its simple sugar pool induces swift elevations in blood glucose, requiring precise pancreatic beta-cell insulin response management in diabetic patients.

Surface Cuticular Adhesion and Exogenous Microflora Accumulation: The sticky, fructose-saturated outer epicarp acts as an active adhesive matrix for environmental dust, fungal spores, and bacterial contaminants, demanding thorough fluid decontamination prior to oral ingestion.
